results.question: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?

plan.restated_question: Which hubs in the Midwest are most exposed to winter disruption?

results.answer: Minneapolis and Chicago are the Midwest hubs most exposed to winter disruption on the 0-100 scale (2016-2025). Minneapolis leads with a winter score of 56.3 (#1 of 5 Midwest hubs; #4 of 10 overall across all hazards), driven by 40.39 measurable snow days/yr (>= 0.25 cm, #2 of 10), 23.7 extreme-cold days/yr (min <= -18 C / 0 F, #1 of 10), and 5.5 heavy-snow days/yr (>= 5 cm, #1 of 10). Chicago ranks second at 37.8 (#2 of 5 Midwest hubs; #2 of 10 overall), with 32.7 measurable snow days/yr (#3 of 10), 4.1 heavy-snow days/yr (tied #2 of 10), and 7.2 extreme-cold days/yr (#2 of 10). Columbus follows at 25.5 (#3 of 5 Midwest hubs; #8 of 10 overall), led by 25.2 measurable snow days/yr (#4 of 10) and 0.4 likely freezing-rain/ice days/yr (tied #2 of 10). Kansas City scores 24.5 (#4 of 5 Midwest hubs; #3 of 10 overall) despite ranking #1 of 10 in likely freezing-rain/ice days (0.5 days/yr). Indianapolis is lowest at 18.1 (#5 of 5 Midwest hubs; #9 of 10 overall), with 19.6 measurable snow days/yr (#5 of 10).
caveats: Open-Meteo is modeled data: absolute snow totals run low, so hub rankings are more reliable than absolute values.

Under the noisy-OR overall score—where high risk in one hazard is not offset by lower risk elsewhere—Houston is 100.0 (#1 of 10), saturated by its hurricane score, while Miami is 69.7 (#5 of 10).
